hook: Freelancing on the side? Your personal savings may be on the hook for business debts.

blocks.narration: Freelancing on the side? Your personal savings may be on the hook for business debts. Here is what an LLC changes.
blocks.visual: Bold poster-style graphic of two doors, one plain, one with a shield emblem, orange and navy palette

blocks.narration: If you start selling or freelancing on your own, you are automatically a sole proprietor. No paperwork needed in most cases.
blocks.visual: A figure walks through the plain door and a tiny shop appears instantly

blocks.narration: It is simple and cheap, but there is no wall between you and the business. Business debts can reach your personal savings.
blocks.visual: A crack opens between the tiny shop and a house, coins sliding across

blocks.narration: A limited liability company creates a separate legal entity. Done properly, it can help shield personal assets from business debts and lawsuits.
blocks.visual: A glowing wall rises between the shop and the house, coins staying on the shop side

blocks.narration: Taxes usually do not change at first. By default, a single-member LLC is taxed just like a sole proprietorship.
blocks.visual: Two identical tax envelopes slide out from behind both doors

blocks.narration: The protection is not automatic though. Mixing personal and business money, or skipping state filings, can seriously weaken it in court.
blocks.visual: The wall flickers as personal and business coins get tossed into the same jar

blocks.narration: Forming an LLC also means paying state filing fees and sometimes yearly fees, which vary widely from state to state.
blocks.visual: A small map of states with price tags of different sizes popping up

blocks.narration: Start simple, and upgrade when the risk or income grows. Save this for when your side hustle starts growing.
blocks.visual: The plain door transforms into the shield door as the shop grows bigger

cta: Save this for when your side hustle starts growing.

captions.hook_line: LLC or sole proprietor? What actually changes for your side hustle 🏢
captions.body: A sole proprietorship is automatic and simple but offers no separation between you and the business. An LLC can help protect personal assets from business debts and lawsuits, and by default a single-member LLC is taxed like a sole proprietorship. State fees vary. Not legal advice.

youtube_title: LLC vs Sole Proprietor: What Actually Changes
